newsitem.title: USA: Texans support governor's tax plan - poll.
newsitem.headline: Texans support governor's tax plan - poll.

text.p: A majority of Texans supported Gov. George Bush's plan to cut property taxes by nearly $3 billion and raise the state sales tax, according to a poll released over the weekend.

Six in ten Texans polled said they were in favor of the property tax relief plan, which would boost the state sales tax one-half cent to 6.75 percent and use $1 billion of the state's budget surplus to offset the reduced property taxes, the Houston Chronicle reported Sunday.

In the Harte-Hanks Texas Poll, 59 percent of the Texans specifically said they would be willing to pay higher sales taxes if it reduced property taxes in the state. The poll of 998 adult Texans was conducted Feb. 2-15 and had a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.

The plan to cut property taxes and raise sales taxes to fund local schools was met with sharp criticism in the state legislature. Critics said Bush proposed the property tax cuts as a high-profile issue for vaulting into the race for the Republican presidential nomination in 2000.
In the poll, nearly seven in ten Texans said they thought Gov. Bush's performance was excellent or good, while 25 percent characterized his performance as fair or poor.
